rules: Only absolute http/https URLs; reject URL userinfo.
Disable environment proxy so a proxy cannot resolve outside the policy.
Resolver checks each redirect hop, validates every DNS candidate, rejects a mixed safe/private address set, and passes exact vetted SocketAddrs to connector without re-resolution.

purpose: Serves packaged/debug static files and NodeCompat assets.
internalBootstrapServer.currentConstraints: Loopback 127.0.0.1 ephemeral port; ordinary handler only GET + Connection: close. It is app bootstrap/resource transport, not Node http.createServer/listen. Preserve it if the outbound client is removed.

currentCallers.uses: Calls Niva.stream("http.requestStream") directly; it does not use browser fetch or the unary Niva.api.http override.
Maps Niva.api.http.get/post/request onto the same Native requestStream.

Exercises Niva.api.http.get/request/post; api-test-matrix.md records all three.

minimum: Connect to vetted address or bind/listen/accept.
Stable per-socket handle/connection ID and per-connection cancellation.
Binary read chunks and binary writes with queue/backpressure result.
Half-close/end, full destroy/close, EOF, error and timeout events with stable ordering.
Peer/local address and port; caller cannot provide an unchecked resolved IP that bypasses Rust destination policy.
minimumNativePrimitiveContract.layering: JS owns Node Socket/Server, HTTP/1.1 parsing, headers, request/response events and stream semantics over this byte transport.
minimumNativePrimitiveContract.security: Hostname resolution and address authorization must remain Rust-side before connect; connect to the exact vetted SocketAddr without a second DNS resolution.

minimum: Send one datagram to an authorized peer and receive datagram boundaries plus remote/local address.
Per-socket events, cancellation, errors and bounded receive queues.
If multicast/broadcast APIs are included, add explicit Native option and destination policy.
minimumNativePrimitiveContract.layering: JS DNS packet encoding/decoding and Node dgram Socket behavior can sit above UDP primitives. DNS traffic may need an explicit permitted resolver endpoint policy; do not treat arbitrary RFC1918 destinations as allowed.

minimum: Wrap a connected TCP stream for client handshake and a listening/accepted stream for server handshake.
Validate certificate chain and hostname against an explicit trust policy; preserve SNI and surface handshake/certificate errors.
Server certificates/private keys supplied through an explicit configuration path.
Expose decrypted bytes through the same bounded read/write/half-close/backpressure/cancel contract.
If Node baseline includes ALPN/session options, implement or explicitly reject them.
minimumNativePrimitiveContract.layering: JS implements Node tls.TLSSocket semantics and HTTPS protocol over TLS streams; Native retains cryptographic handshake and certificate validation.
minimumNativePrimitiveContract.security: Do not disable verification by default. Address filtering remains in the Native TCP connect path before TLS starts.

Moving NodeCompat alone is insufficient because Devtools checkVersion and public Niva.api.http examples/tests still call it.
otherBlockers: Current Native public Niva.api.http.get/request/post contract and existing tests/examples.
Browser Fetch changes CORS/CSP and request/response semantics; JS code cannot enforce the existing resolved-address denylist.
If raw TCP client is used instead, Native connect must preserve URL validation, redirect-hop revalidation and vetted-address/no-re-resolve policy.

capability.summary: Encodes/decodes DNS question/response wire packets and TCP length-prefixed packet framing. It does not open sockets, query configured DNS servers, use OS resolver/search configuration, follow CNAMEs, cache, retry, timeout, or implement Node dns.lookup/resolve semantics.

browserViability.bufferDependency: dns-packet/index.js uses require("buffer").Buffer; esbuild platform=browser resolved this to the pinned pure-JS npm buffer@6.0.3 package already present in the temp project.

limitations: Bundle size is for the full CommonJS codec export object after browser bundling; it includes Buffer polyfill and ip-codec but excludes socket/resolver logic.
The package has no browser field; bundlers must resolve its Node buffer import to a browser Buffer implementation. The measured build uses buffer@6.0.3.

Niva currently has its own Buffer implementation; compatibility with the feross Buffer instance used by this bundle requires a shared Buffer alias or explicit Uint8Array/Buffer conversion at packet and socket boundaries. This was not runtime-tested.

dns.lookup remains an OS resolver/API concern. dns.resolve and dns.resolve4 still need a configured server/transport strategy (for example the planned dgram/net path or another chosen transport); packet encoding alone does not complete them.
No API runtime tests, socket tests, WebView platform checks, or release size builds were run. gzip/DEFLATE numbers are Node zlib level 6 and may differ from Niva packaging implementation.

rustDns.reviewScope: Read-only assessment of Rust dns-packet 0.1.0 plus an isolated temporary size harness; no Niva source/dependencies/build targets changed.

functionalReview.summary: Small low-level DNS wire reader/writer, not a resolver and not a typed-record codec.
supported: Ordinary resource headers (owner, type, class, TTL, RDLENGTH).
Single compression-pointer hop to a prior uncompressed name; synthetic compressed A answer owner passes.
Writer suffix-compresses a repeated answer owner against the earlier uncompressed question.
Caller can manually decode common A octets, CNAME name RDATA, and length-prefixed TXT chunks.
materialGaps: Reader::read_resource returns only Resource header metadata and leaves the RDATA cursor at payload start; caller must read/validate RDLENGTH and decode each type. Writer::write_resource writes metadata only; caller appends RDATA bytes.

A second compressed name pointing to a prior compressed-pointer owner is rejected; the synthetic two-answer A packet is a passing expected-gap test (reader returns None). Main-thread JS dns-packet 5.6.1 fixture result passes this case.
No RR-type enum or typed RDATA helpers for A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/PTR/SOA/SRV/TXT/etc.
Reader name decoding assumes UTF-8 labels; non-UTF8 DNS label bytes fail.
Writer replaces labels longer than 63 bytes with ___invalid___ rather than returning an error; caller must validate labels.
No UDP/TCP resolver, transaction matching, retries, timeout, response policy or Node DNS error mapping.

sourcePointers.claim: no_std plus alloc String/Vec and optional log
Header/Question/Resource expose wire metadata; Resource has no typed RDATA
compressed-name reader performs one pointer hop and rejects pointer-to-pointer targets
read_resource stops after RDLENGTH; payload remains for caller
writer suffix compression and header-only resource serialization
oversize labels are replaced rather than rejected

Default log feature produced no extra bytes in this specific optimized harness; this is observed here only, not a general guarantee that log is free in Niva.
Measured delta covers reader/writer branches linked by this harness; typed RDATA helpers, DNS resolver/network code, Node API adapters and integration glue are excluded.
